headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line while fear sits mid-range and BTC quietly leaves exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unanimous today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all trading below their 200-day moving averages, and none carries a golden cross. That's not a mixed market, that's a market where every major asset is on the wrong side of its own long-term trend line at the same time. BTC sits 49% off its 12-month high of $124,773, ETH is down 60.6% from its high, and ADA is the worst of the group at -83.2% from its peak. When the whole board agrees on direction, the story isn't which coin to watch, it's that the entire complex is still working through a drawdown.

Momentum tells a subtler story than trend does. RSI readings cluster in the 40s to mid-50s across the board, meaning nobody is stretched in either direction, this is a resting market, not a screaming one. But there are real divergences worth naming. ETH's RSI of 56.3 sits with a 7-day gain of 1.81% and a 30-day gain of 6.36%, yet its MACD is still below signal, price is climbing while the momentum indicator hasn't confirmed it. BNB and DOGE show the opposite tension: both have MACD above signal (a bullish short-term momentum cross) while both remain deep below their 200-day lines and, in DOGE's case, down 19.15% over 30 days. Short-term momentum and long-term trend are pulling in different directions across several of these names, which is exactly the kind of thing that makes a single indicator misleading in isolation.

Positioning adds texture. BTC funding sits at 5.1% annualized, a modest cost for longs to hold their bets, paired with liquidations over the last 24 hours skewed hard toward longs ($5.8M liquidated versus $1.4M of shorts), meaning the recent squeeze has been punishing the long side. DOGE and XRP show the most crowded books: DOGE funding runs 8.3% annualized with a long/short ratio of 4.70, XRP funding 5.5% with a ratio of 3.57. Both are expensive, one-sided bets by the numbers. Yet DOGE's liquidations flipped that script in the last 22 hours, shorts lost $456k versus $146k for longs, an odd wrinkle where the crowded side (longs, per the ratio) wasn't the side getting flushed. SOL stands out with negative funding (-1.1% annualized), shorts are paying longs there even as its long/short ratio of 2.3 says more accounts are positioned long. Crowded and cheap is a different animal than crowded and expensive, and SOL's book right now reads as the former.

On flows, the picture splits into two windows worth stating separately. Bitcoin ETFs saw a $7.8M net inflow on August 11th, but that single day followed a run where the same_direction_days count of 1 tells us this was a fresh flip, not a continuation, even though the trailing five-session net for BTC ETFs was a healthy +$346.9M. Ether ETFs show the inverse tension: the latest day (Aug 11) printed a net outflow of $1.7M, and same_direction_days of 2 means the last two sessions have leaned negative together, yet the five-session net for ETH ETFs is still positive at +$186.2M, meaning the earlier days in that window did the heavy lifting. Read plainly: ETH ETF demand has cooled over the most recent two sessions even as the broader five-day tally remains positive. Whale wallets, meanwhile, moved $180.8M net off exchanges in the last 24 hours, all of it BTC, with $128.9M leaving Kraken and $51.9M leaving Coinbase Institutional. But the four-session trend behind that (-$190M, +$1,180M, +$1,125M, -$693M) shows this isn't a straight line either, two big off-exchange days were followed by a sharp $693M move back onto exchanges before today's smaller off-exchange print. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, sits at $306.4B, down 0.98% over the last 30 days, a mild contraction rather than a buildup.

Set against all that, the Fear & Greed index reads 27, labeled Fear, which sits comfortably inside its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. That's not panic, it's the same low-grade unease that's been the background for a month. The tension worth sitting with is that this sentiment gauge has barely moved while the tape underneath it has produced real, if noisy, signals: longs getting liquidated in BTC, a fresh but unconfirmed BTC ETF inflow, a cooling two-day stretch in ETH ETF flows, and whale wallets pulling BTC off exchanges on net today after a choppy few sessions. None of these threads agree cleanly with each other, and none of them agree cleanly with a sentiment reading that's been flat for weeks.

What to watch from here: whether BTC's ETF flow turns into more than one same-direction day, whether ETH ETF flows extend their two-day negative streak into the five-session number, and whether any major reclaims its 200-day line, which would be the first crack in an otherwise uniform sub-200-day board. A shift in funding sign on DOGE or XRP away from their current premiums, or a reversal in the whale exchange-flow trend back toward sustained inflows, would also be worth noting as a change in the conditions described here.
